defects.finding: Four rendered meta descriptions exceeded 160 characters.
defects.rootCause: Legal document description fields were written as broad summaries rather than search-result descriptions.
defects.fix: Shortened the legal metadata descriptions without changing legal document text.
defects.verification: check-meta-lengths.mjs: 105 pages checked, 0 descriptions over 160, 0 titles over 60.

defects.finding: Legacy legal aliases duplicated canonical legal H1s and carried self-canonical URLs despite being noindex.
defects.rootCause: Aliases were noindex but did not consolidate canonical signals or redirect to the maintained legal route.
defects.fix: Alias metadata now canonicalizes to /legal/* with noindex,follow; the Worker issues permanent 301 redirects to the maintained legal pages.
defects.verification: Worker redirect test covers all six legacy routes; strict SEO audit reports 0 canonical collisions.

defects.finding: Two legacy static HTML pages remained indexable while the production Worker redirected them.
defects.rootCause: Redirect metadata was not aligned with the edge redirect behavior.
defects.fix: Both fallback pages are now noindex,follow and canonicalize to their final destinations.
defects.verification: Strict audit reports 0 indexable pages missing from sitemap and 0 noindex pages included in sitemap.

defects.finding: The export had 97 pages marked indexable while sitemap.xml contained only 94 URLs; the human sitemap page was omitted and redirect fallbacks were incorrectly indexable.
defects.rootCause: No strict machine comparison existed between rendered indexability and the generated sitemap.
defects.fix: Added the human sitemap route, corrected redirect fallback robots directives, and added a strict indexability/sitemap parity gate.
defects.verification: Strict audit: 95 indexable routes, 95 sitemap URLs, 0 hard errors, 0 warnings.

defects.finding: Several pages published BreadcrumbList JSON-LD without a corresponding visible breadcrumb trail.
defects.rootCause: Structured-data helpers were added before every template exposed the same breadcrumb UI.
defects.fix: Added optional breadcrumbs to PageHero and visible breadcrumb trails to the affected templates, including article pages.
defects.verification: Strict audit parses every JSON-LD block and verifies page-specific FAQ, article, breadcrumb, and person content against rendered text: 0 errors.

defects.finding: The homepage title was only the brand name 'CertaMaris' and did not state the product category.
defects.rootCause: The root layout default title was used without a homepage-specific metadata export.
defects.fix: Added homepage metadata using 'Maritime Cyber Compliance Software — CertaMaris' and the approved site description.
defects.verification: Rendered homepage title is 44 characters and remains unique.

defects.finding: The founder portrait was declared as a 1200x630 PNG social image, but the actual asset is a 1251x1361 JPEG.
defects.rootCause: A portrait was passed through a helper that assumed a standard landscape social-card image.
defects.fix: Leadership now uses the approved branded social card; the shared helper infers image MIME type and only supplies default dimensions for standard OG PNG cards.
defects.verification: All rendered OG image paths resolve; root social-card QA remains 14/14 PASS.

defects.finding: Existing SEO checks did not compare sitemap membership to rendered indexability, validate JSON-LD against visible content, detect canonical collisions, or crawl the full sitemap visually.
defects.rootCause: SEO QA focused on title presence and uniqueness rather than cross-system integrity.
defects.fix: Added seo-audit.mjs and seo-visual-qa.mjs, integrated strict SEO audit and meta-length checks into npm run qa, and added full-sitemap screenshot, H1, overflow, image, console, and network checks.
defects.verification: Strict audit, 95-route visual crawl, and all existing repository gates pass.

knownResiduals: No Search Console or analytics export was available, so no traffic, query, indexing, ranking, or click-through claims are made.
Legacy legal aliases remain available as static noindex fallbacks but redirect to maintained legal routes in production.
No keyword-volume, difficulty, competitor-gap, or backlink data was fabricated or inferred.
